paras.en: "The OPEC+ group of seven kept their production ceilings unchanged, in line with market expectations. That said, despite rising flows through the Strait of Hormuz, their output levels remain well below quota," said UBS analyst Giovanni Staunovo.
paras.zh: “OPEC+七国集团维持产量上限不变，符合市场预期。尽管如此，尽管通过霍尔木兹海峡的流量有所增加，但其产量水平仍远低于配额，”瑞银分析师乔瓦尼·斯塔诺沃(Giovanni Staunovo)表示。

paras.en: "Consequently, the oil market remains tight."
paras.zh: “因此，石油市场仍然紧张。”

paras.en: Oil prices had dropped on Friday after European leaders agreed to U.S. President Donald Trump's request to release diesel reserves. Crude oil prices settled lower after the Group of Seven nations announced the release of diesel and crude stocks to ease surging fuel prices.
paras.zh: 在欧洲领导人同意美国总统唐纳德·特朗普释放柴油储备的请求后，周五油价下跌。在七国集团宣布释放柴油和原油库存以缓解飙升的燃料价格后，原油价格走低。

paras.en: International benchmark Brent crude futures slipped 6 cents to close at $102.25 per barrel, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude slid $1.76 to $91.11 a barrel.
paras.zh: 国际基准布伦特原油期货下跌 6 美分，收于每桶 102.25 美元，而美国西德克萨斯中质原油下跌 1.76 美元，收于每桶 91.11 美元。

paras.en: The G7 will release 100 million barrels of reserves over the next four months "with a frontloaded substantial diesel release within the first 20 days," the group's leaders said in a joint statement. The G7 includes France, Canada, Germany, Italy, Japan, the United Kingdom and the U.S.
paras.zh: 七国集团领导人在一份联合声明中表示，七国集团领导人将在未来四个月内释放 1 亿桶储备，“并在头 20 天内提前释放大量柴油”。七国集团包括法国、加拿大、德国、意大利、日本、英国和美国。

paras.en: Despite the G7 announcement, Brent crude remains above $100 a barrel, up from about $73 before the Iran war started in late February.
paras.zh: 尽管七国集团宣布了这一消息，但布伦特原油仍高于每桶 100 美元，高于 2 月底伊朗战争爆发前的约 73 美元。

paras.en: The Iran war has also delayed the group's output capacity review — crucial to determine members' 2027 output quotas — because it has thrown estimates of future production potential into uncertainty, industry sources told Reuters last week.
paras.zh: 行业消息人士上周告诉路透社，伊朗战争还推迟了该组织的产能审查——这对于确定成员国2027年的产量配额至关重要——因为它使对未来生产潜力的估计陷入不确定性。

paras.en: OPEC+ has been raising output targets for much of 2026 after years of production cuts, but most of the increases stayed on paper because of the Middle East conflict.
paras.zh: 经过多年减产后，OPEC+一直在提高2026年大部分时间的产量目标，但由于中东冲突，大部分增产目标仍停留在纸面上。

paras.en: The seven core OPEC+ members pumped 25 million barrels per day in August, up 630,000 bpd from July, yet still roughly 5 million bpd below prewar levels in February, OPEC data shows.
paras.zh: OPEC 数据显示，OPEC+ 七个核心成员国 8 月份日产量为 2500 万桶，较 7 月份增加 63 万桶，但仍比 2 月份战前水平低约 500 万桶。

paras.en: OPEC+ still has about 2 million bpd of output cuts in place covering most members. It needs the result of the capacity review to decide how to distribute increases, and any changes to output are unlikely before 2027, sources have said.
paras.zh: OPEC+ 仍实施约 200 万桶/日的减产计划，涵盖大多数成员国。消息人士称，需要根据产能审查的结果来决定如何分配增量，并且在 2027 年之前不太可能对产量做出任何改变。

paras.en: A separate OPEC+ ministerial group, the Joint Ministerial Monitoring Committee, which does not set policy, also met on Sunday to review the market.
paras.zh: 一个单独的欧佩克+部长级小组，即联合部长级监测委员会，不制定政策，也在周日举行会议以审查市场。

articles.title: This NYC startup requires 4 days in office but just let everyone work remote for a whole month

paras.en: Bruno Solari spent his August traveling all around Spain, starting with a week in Ibiza, continuing on to Madrid, Málaga, Marbella and Barcelona, before finally returning to Ibiza for a bachelor party.
paras.zh: 布鲁诺·索拉里 (Bruno Solari) 整个八月都在西班牙各地旅行，首先在伊维萨岛待一周，然后继续前往马德里、马拉加、马贝拉和巴塞罗那，最后返回伊维萨岛参加单身派对。

paras.en: He also managed to squeeze in a few meetings and client calls all throughout.
paras.zh: 他还设法在整个过程中挤出了一些会议和客户电话。

paras.en: Solari, founder and CEO of the New York City-based PR firm SolComms, was among his company's 53 employees enjoying their inaugural "Work from Anywhere August." Other employees logged on from all over the U.S. (the Jersey Shore, the Hamptons, Florida) and the world (Berlin, Prague, London, Portugal).
paras.zh: Solari 是总部位于纽约市的公关公司 SolComms 的创始人兼首席执行官，他的公司有 53 名员工，他们正在享受首次“八月随时随地工作”活动。其他员工从美国各地（泽西海岸、汉普顿、佛罗里达）和世界各地（柏林、布拉格、伦敦、葡萄牙）登录。

paras.en: "I was in Spain the entire month of August, and I would have felt like a hypocrite if I was going to be there and making my team be in-office," Solari, 33, tells CNBC Make It. "So I thought, 'OK, I'm doing this myself. I'm going to grant that flexibility to the entire agency.'"
paras.zh: 33 岁的索拉里告诉 CNBC Make It，“整个 8 月我都在西班牙，如果我要去那里并让我的团队上任，我会觉得自己像个伪君子。” “所以我想，‘好吧，我自己做这件事。我将向整个机构提供这种灵活性。’”

paras.en: The end-of-summer experiment felt like a worthwhile risk to the 3-year-old startup: Employee surveys of the trial indicate boosted productivity, work-life balance and happiness, while the business also saw a modest revenue boost. It also runs counter to several big companies scaling back on remote-work flexibility in a job market where employers have the upper hand.
paras.zh: 对于这家成立 3 年的初创公司来说，夏末的实验感觉是一次值得冒险的尝试：该实验的员工调查显示，生产力、工作与生活的平衡和幸福感得到了提高，同时公司的收入也出现了适度的增长。这也与几家大公司在雇主占上风的就业市场上缩减远程工作灵活性的做法背道而驰。

paras.en: "I think people were surprised that I went for it," Solari says.
paras.zh: “我认为人们对我的努力感到惊讶，”索拉里说。

paras.en: Four weeks of fully remote work from anywhere in the world is a bold move for the millennial founder, who came up in PR agencies at the height of the hustle culture era and says he holds more "traditional" workplace values, like building company culture through in-person interactions rather than "through a screen" of fully remote work. Since its founding in 2023, SolComms has operated with a four days in-office requirement, with Fridays at home that end at 3 p.m. most weeks (and 12 p.m. during the summer).
paras.zh: 对于这位千禧一代创始人来说，在世界任何地方进行四个星期的完全远程工作是一个大胆的举动，他在喧嚣文化时代的鼎盛时期进入公关机构，并表示自己持有更“传统”的工作场所价值观，比如通过面对面的互动而不是“通过屏幕”完全远程工作来建立公司文化。自 2023 年成立以来，SolComms 一直要求在办公室工作四天，周五在家办公，直到下午 3 点结束。大多数星期（夏季中午 12 点）。

paras.en: Some 25% of full-time U.S. workers work in a hybrid arrangement, with the most common requirements being three days in the office, followed by four, according to a recent report from Owl Labs, a video-conferencing technology company, which surveyed 2,000 people in July. Most, 65%, work onsite full time, and 10% work remotely full time.
paras.zh: 视频会议技术公司 Owl Labs 在 7 月份对 2000 名员工进行了调查，报告显示，大约 25% 的美国全职员工采取混合工作方式，最常见的要求是在办公室工作三天，其次是四天。大多数人（65%）全职在现场工作，10% 则全职远程工作。

paras.en: Solari says every year his company surveys its own employees about the perks and benefits they want, and every year they ask for more work-from-home days. Wary of granting another remote working day during the week, Solari thought to offer 100% flexibility within a one-month period instead.
paras.zh: 索拉里说，他的公司每年都会对员工进行调查，了解他们想要的福利和福利，每年他们都会要求增加在家工作的时间。由于担心在一周内再提供一个远程工作日，Solari 考虑在一个月内提供 100% 的灵活性。

paras.en: He and his leadership team came up with the idea in January, announced it to employees in February, and spent the next six months coming up with best practices to make sure everyone was set up for remote success.
paras.zh: 他和他的领导团队在一月份提出了这个想法，并在二月份向员工宣布了这一想法，并在接下来的六个月里提出了最佳实践，以确保每个人都为远程成功做好了准备。

paras.en: Among those guidelines: Stick to 9 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. EST working hours, keep cameras on for all meetings, dress for meetings as if you were going into the office, use Slack status updates liberally, take lunch and other breaks, and no sensitive calls or screens in public spaces.
paras.zh: 这些准则包括：坚持上午 9 点至下午 5:30。美国东部时间工作时间，在所有会议上保持摄像头开着，参加会议时着装就像要进入办公室一样，自由使用 Slack 状态更新，吃午饭和其他休息时间，并且在公共场所禁止敏感电话或屏幕。

paras.en: SolComms also communicated their remote-August plans to the agency's 80-plus clients across healthcare, tech and AI, and consumer brands, says Natalie Valicenti, 30, the company's associate vice president of operations, who split her remote month across Rhode Island and Minnesota.
paras.zh: SolComms 运营副总裁 30 岁的娜塔莉·瓦利琴蒂 (Natalie Valicenti) 表示，该公司还向该机构的 80 多家医疗保健、科技和人工智能以及消费品牌客户传达了他们的远程 8 月计划，她将远程月的时间分配到了罗德岛州和明尼苏达州。

paras.en: The SolComms benefit comes at a time when many company leaders are scaling back on employee flexibility and benefits, and during a tightening labor market where employers have the upper-hand.
paras.zh: SolComms 的福利出台之际，许多公司领导者都在缩减员工的灵活性和福利，而且劳动力市场趋紧，而雇主占据了上风。

paras.en: In September, Uber announced plans to cut about 3,300 corporate jobs, as well as scale down its remote workforce and tighten in-office rules. Disney said it would require more employees to report to the office four days a week and later announced layoffs of about 300 employees.
paras.zh: 9 月，Uber 宣布计划裁员约 3,300 个企业岗位，并缩减远程员工规模并收紧办公室规定。迪士尼表示，将要求更多员工每周四天到办公室报到，随后又宣布裁员约 300 名员工。

paras.en: The five-day return-to-office creep has been growing for several years. The share of Fortune 500 companies requiring five days in the office nearly doubled from mid-2024 to mid-2025, from 13% to 24%, according to research from Flex Index, a resource within the advisory firm Work Forward that analyzes office requirements data.
paras.zh: 五天重返办公室的现象多年来一直在增长。 Flex Index 的研究显示，从 2024 年中期到 2025 年中期，需要在办公室工作五天的财富 500 强公司的比例几乎翻了一番，从 13% 增至 24%。Flex Index 是咨询公司 Work Forward 内分析办公室需求数据的资源。

paras.en: But for SolComms, the risks of loosening office requirements for a month seem to have paid off.
paras.zh: 但对于 SolComms 来说，放松一个月办公要求的风险似乎已经得到了回报。

paras.en: Twenty-one employees answered a survey following the inaugural remote month, with 76% saying they were more productive, 90% saying they maintained high work-life balance, and 100% saying they want Work from Anywhere August back next year, according to documents reviewed by Make It. Several say the experience helped them strengthen their communication and self-management skills, and a lot of people said cutting their commute times was the biggest draw.
paras.zh: 根据 Make It 查阅的文件，在第一个远程月份结束后，有 21 名员工接受了一项调查，其中 76% 的员工表示自己的工作效率更高，90% 的员工表示自己保持了工作与生活的高度平衡，100% 的员工表示希望明年 8 月恢复“随处工作”。一些人表示，这段经历帮助他们加强了沟通和自我管理技能，很多人表示，减少通勤时间是最大的吸引力。

paras.en: There were also some downsides, like staffers saying they felt tied to their computers and found it hard to step away, whereas it felt more natural to take breaks for lunch, coffee or a walk if they were in the office.
paras.zh: 也有一些缺点，比如员工们表示，他们感觉被电脑束缚住了，很难离开，而如果他们在办公室，吃午饭、喝咖啡或散步会感觉更自然。

paras.en: Solari says he sees this "internal pressure to be available" as a common struggle with remote work.
paras.zh: 索拉里表示，他认为这种“可用的内部压力”是远程工作的常见问题。

paras.en: "I think it's a matter of continuing to let employees know that we're flexible," he says. "You don't need to be chained to a desk to prove that you're doing a good job, and ultimately, it's not always the person who's the first to respond who's the power player in producing results."
paras.zh: “我认为问题在于继续让员工知道我们是灵活的，”他说。 “你不需要被锁在办公桌上来证明你做得很好，最终，并不总是第一个做出回应的人才是产生结果的权力参与者。”

paras.en: Though not the goal, Solari says, the business also saw financial benefits: Revenue increased by a modest 4% revenue from July to August, and jumped 12% from August to September.
paras.zh: 索拉里表示，尽管这不是目标，但该公司也看到了财务效益：7 月至 8 月的收入小幅增长了 4%，8 月至 9 月的收入增长了 12%。

paras.en: Solari is already committed to a return of the program in August 2027.
paras.zh: Solari 已承诺于 2027 年 8 月恢复该计划。

paras.en: "[We're] 1,000% doing it again, without a doubt," he says.
paras.zh: “毫无疑问，[我们] 1,000% 会再次这样做，”他说。

articles.title: NASA directive might increase the odds of contaminating Mars

paras.en: A new NASA directive seeks to loosen “planetary protection” rules meant to avoid the contamination other worlds with microbial life from Earth.
paras.zh: 美国宇航局的一项新指令旨在放宽“行星保护”规则，旨在避免来自地球的微生物生命污染其他世界。

paras.en: The policy shift arrived via a message to NASA personnel that was obtained and shared yesterday by the independent watchdog sites NASA Watch and Astrobiology.com. In it, NASA administrator Jared Isaacman writes that procedures for avoiding contamination “must reflect our current scientific knowledge” and argues that this knowledge has shifted since the current rules were established decades ago.
paras.zh: 这一政策转变是通过独立监管网站 NASA Watch 和 Astrobiology.com 昨天获得并分享的一条发给 NASA 人员的消息实现的。美国宇航局局长贾里德·艾萨克曼在其中写道，避免污染的程序“必须反映我们当前的科学知识”，并认为自几十年前制定现行规则以来，这种知识已经发生了变化。

paras.en: The directive “ensures we can use our incredible data to lower costs on our missions,” says Nicky Fox, associate administrator of NASA’s Science Mission Directorate. “This process will also help increase commercial capabilities—getting more missions into space by streamlining space exploration.”
paras.zh: NASA 科学任务理事会副局长尼基·福克斯 (Nicky Fox) 表示，该指令“确保我们能够利用令人难以置信的数据来降低任务成本”。 “这一过程还将有助于提高商业能力——通过简化太空探索，将更多任务送入太空。”

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: In 1964 members of the International Council for Science’s Committee on Space Research (COSPAR), led by the United Nations–affiliated International Council of Scientific Unions (now the International Science Council), feared that the breakneck pace of the space race could lead to spacecraft accidentally contaminating alien worlds with microbial life from Earth. If those interplanetary hitchhikers were sufficiently resilient and numerous to form self-sustaining populations on Mars or other planets, they could forever alter those otherwise-pristine environments and sabotage all future efforts to discover true alien life there. So COSPAR issued a resolution that any mission to another potentially habitable or inhabited world must demonstrate a less than one-in-10,000 chance of exposing such places to terrestrial life capable of interplanetary colonization.
paras.zh: 1964 年，由联合国附属国际科学联盟理事会（现为国际科学理事会）领导的国际科学理事会空间研究委员会 (COSPAR) 的成员担心，太空竞赛的惊人速度可能会导致航天器意外地让来自地球的微生物污染外星世界。如果这些星际搭便车的人有足够的弹性和数量，能够在火星或其他行星上形成自给自足的种群，他们就可以永远改变那些原本原始的环境，并破坏未来所有在那里发现真正的外星生命的努力。因此，COSPAR 发布了一项决议，要求任何前往另一个可能适宜居住或有人居住的世界的任务都必须证明，将这些地方暴露于能够进行星际殖民的地球生命的可能性低于万分之一。

paras.en: The new directive notes that COSPAR subsequently tightened those rules to account for the flurry of Mars-bound missions, some carrying human crews, that were widely expected to launch in the intervening decades. Codified in 1969, those more stringent and costly restrictions have guided—and greatly limited, some critics say—Mars exploration ever since. But “human exploration did not progress as quickly as all believed,” Isaacman’s message reads, while technology for sterilizing spacecraft has improved markedly. “Our long-standing policies were designed in a different era,” he writes.
paras.zh: 新指令指出，空间研究委员会随后收紧了这些规则，以应对一系列前往火星的任务，其中一些载人航天器，人们普遍预计这些任务将在接下来的几十年内发射。这些更严格、成本更高的限制自 1969 年制定以来一直指导着火星探索，一些批评者称，这些限制也极大地限制了火星探索。但艾萨克曼的信息中写道，“人类探索的进展并不像所有人想象的那么快”，而航天器消毒技术却有了显着进步。 “我们的长期政策是在不同的时代制定的，”他写道。

paras.en: Now, the message states, NASA’s rules will immediately be restored to the looser 1964 restriction of less than a one-in-10,000 chance of biocontamination for each Mars-bound mission. And in the meantime, NASA officials will perform a rapid-fire “modernization assessment” of the current science and technology concerning contamination risk, with a December 2026 deadline for delivering recommendations to lower that threshold even further.
paras.zh: 现在，消息称，NASA 的规则将立即恢复到 1964 年较为宽松的限制，即每次火星任务发生生物污染的可能性低于万分之一。与此同时，NASA 官员将对当前有关污染风险的科学技术进行快速“现代化评估”，并在 2026 年 12 月的最后期限内提出进一步降低该阈值的建议。

paras.en: Cassie Conley, NASA’s former (and longest-serving) planetary protection officer, is critical of the change. Given how little we still know about possible life on Mars, she says, relaxing biological contamination constraints now is “idiocy.”
paras.zh: 美国宇航局前（也是任职时间最长的）行星保护官员卡西·康利（Cassie Conley）对这一变化持批评态度。她说，考虑到我们对火星上可能存在的生命仍然知之甚少，现在放松生物污染限制是“愚蠢的”。

paras.en: “I used to point out that planetary protection was probably the first time in history that humans had grown up enough, together as a global species, to decide not to do irreversible and possibly stupid things before we understood the consequences,” she says. “Too bad it didn’t last.”
paras.zh: “我曾经指出，行星保护可能是历史上第一次，人类作为一个全球物种，已经足够成熟，在我们了解后果之前决定不做不可逆转的、可能愚蠢的事情，”她说。 “可惜没能坚持下去。”

paras.en: In a statement shared with Scientific American, NASA clarified that, with the new directive, the agency isn’t weakening existing planetary protection protocols so much as updating them. “This directive moves NASA toward a quantitative, performance-based approach that measures actual contamination risk and applies protections accordingly,” the statement said. Additionally, missions looking for past or present life will “continue to carry requirements appropriate to protecting those investigations.”
paras.zh: 在与《科学美国人》分享的一份声明中，美国宇航局澄清说，通过新指令，该机构并不是在削弱现有的行星保护协议，而是在更新它们。声明称：“这项指令促使美国宇航局采取一种定量的、基于绩效的方法，衡量实际的污染风险并采取相应的保护措施。”此外，寻找过去或现在生命的任务将“继续满足保护这些调查的适当要求”。

paras.en: Such cautions are crucial, experts say, especially because NASA’s Perseverance rover on Mars has uncovered tantalizing hints of possible ancient biosignatures in some of the rocks it has studied. Samples from those rocks are now in limbo, awaiting an as-yet-unclear ride back to Earth for further analysis.
paras.zh: 专家表示，这种谨慎至关重要，特别是因为美国宇航局在火星上的毅力号火星车在其研究的一些岩石中发现了可能存在古代生物特征的诱人线索。这些岩石的样本目前处于悬而未决的状态，等待着返回地球进行进一步分析，但目前情况尚不清楚。

paras.en: “We are actively seeking to learn if the organics we have found on Mars are biological in origin,” says Linday Hays, NASA’s senior scientist for Mars exploration. This policy change will not threaten that goal, she says, but “will allow us to bring decades of science from our Mars exploration to help make our processes more straightforward for robotic and, in the future, human exploration of the Red Planet.”
paras.zh: “我们正在积极寻求了解我们在火星上发现的有机物是否起源于生物，”美国宇航局火星探索高级科学家林迪·海斯说。她说，这一政策变化不会威胁到这一目标，但“将使我们能够利用数十年的火星探索科学成果，帮助我们的流程更加简单，适合机器人以及未来人类对这颗红色星球的探索。”

articles.title: Archaeologists unearth a ‘major’ early Christian monastery in Scotland

paras.en: The earliest days of Christianity are hazy—relatively few written records survive from this era, and religious artifacts are rare archaeological finds. Still, a newly discovered early Christian monastery, dating to just six centuries after the religion got its start, could offer clues to how the faith spread across the world.
paras.zh: 基督教的早期历史是模糊的——这个时代留下的书面记录相对较少，宗教文物也是罕见的考古发现。尽管如此，一座新发现的早期基督教修道院的历史可以追溯到该宗教诞生后仅六个世纪，可以为该信仰如何在世界范围内传播提供线索。

paras.en: In a new study published this week in the journal Antiquity, researchers describe how a group of historians helped discover the early medieval monastery in a stroke of good luck.
paras.zh: 在本周《古代》杂志上发表的一项新研究中，研究人员描述了一群历史学家如何幸运地帮助发现了这座中世纪早期的修道院。

paras.en: The site is situated on the island of Lismore and is believed to have been founded by Saint Mo Luóc, an early Christian saint also known as Moluag. Researchers had long suspected Mo Luóc’s monastery was there but hadn’t been able to prove it until the local Lismore Historical Society led an excavation in the area, which also holds the ruins of a 13th-century cathedral.
paras.zh: 该遗址位于利斯莫尔岛，据信是由早期基督教圣人圣莫卢克 (Saint Mo Luóc) 建立的，也称为莫卢阿格 (Moluag)。研究人员长期以来一直怀疑莫洛克修道院就在那里，但一直未能证明这一点，直到当地利斯莫尔历史学会在该地区领导了一次发掘，该地区还拥有一座 13 世纪大教堂的废墟。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: With the help of professional archaeologists, the historians uncovered ancient grave sites, buildings, pieces of sculpture and extensive evidence of craft workshops at the site.
paras.zh: 在专业考古学家的帮助下，历史学家在现场发现了古代墓地、建筑物、雕塑作品和大量手工作坊的证据。

paras.en: Gordon Noble, the paper’s senior author and an archaeologist at the University of Aberdeen in Scotland, says that the evidence of craftworking is particularly exciting. The team found hundreds of clay molds and crucibles used for working bronze, silver and gold—a somewhat “unusual” find for a monastery, Noble says.
paras.zh: 该论文的资深作者、苏格兰阿伯丁大学的考古学家戈登·诺贝尔表示，手工艺的证据尤其令人兴奋。诺布尔说，研究小组发现了数百个用于加工青铜、银和金的粘土模具和坩埚，这对于修道院来说有点“不寻常”。

paras.en: “It’s one of the largest metalworking assemblages we have from any site, secular or sacred, in this time period,” he says.
paras.zh: “这是这个时期我们在任何地点（无论是世俗还是神圣）所拥有的最大的金属加工组合之一，”他说。

paras.en: Overall, the size of the monastery suggests Lismore, which lies on Loch Linnhe on Scotland’s west coast, was likely more important to medieval Christian society than previously realized, he says.
paras.zh: 他说，总的来说，这座修道院的规模表明，位于苏格兰西海岸林尼湖的利斯莫尔对中世纪基督教社会的重要性可能比之前意识到的更为重要。

paras.en: Other sites are known to have played a major role. For example, the island of Iona, to the southwest of Lismore in Scotland, is known for being the “Cradle of Christianity.” But the new findings suggest Lismore was “a very significant mover and shaker” in the spread of the early religion, Noble says.
paras.zh: 据了解，其他网站也发挥了重要作用。例如，苏格兰利斯莫尔西南部的爱奥那岛以“基督教的摇篮”而闻名。但诺布尔说，新的发现表明利斯莫尔在早期宗教的传播中是“一个非常重要的推动者和震撼者”。

paras.en: Noble and his colleagues plan to keep investigating the site, including an analysis of the monastery’s “vallum,” or outer boundary, often indicated by a wall or bank.
paras.zh: 诺贝尔和他的同事计划继续调查该地点，包括分析修道院的“vallum”或外部边界，通常由墙壁或河岸表示。

paras.en: The entire monastery appears to have been “huge,” Noble says. “It’ll be really exciting to see what shows up in the coming years.”
paras.zh: 诺布尔说，整个修道院似乎“巨大”。 “看到未来几年会出现什么将会非常令人兴奋。”

articles.title: How attachment theory can help us understand AI relationships

paras.en: Attachment is the term psychologists use for the most significant relationships that hold people’s lives together.
paras.zh: 心理学家用“依恋”一词来形容将人们的生活联系在一起的最重要的关系。

paras.en: But what makes an attachment relationship different from all others? According to the pioneering American-Canadian developmental psychologist Mary Ainsworth, it must meet the following six conditions.
paras.zh: 但是依恋关系与其他关系有何不同呢？根据美国加拿大发展心理学家先驱玛丽·安斯沃斯（Mary Ainsworth）的说法，它必须满足以下六个条件。

paras.en: (1) The relationship must persist over time, having (2) been formed with a particular subject who cannot be replaced. (3) The relationship must be emotionally significant, (4) involve the desire to remain close to them, and (5) cause distress at involuntary separation. And finally (6) when threatened, the person must seek security and comfort in their relationship with that subject.
paras.zh: (1) 这种关系必须随着时间的推移持续存在，(2) 是与一个无法替代的特定主体形成的。 (3) 这种关系必须在情感上具有重要意义，(4) 包含与他们保持亲密关系的愿望，以及 (5) 在非自愿分离时造成痛苦。最后（6）当受到威胁时，该人必须在与该主体的关系中寻求安全感和安慰。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: The first five conditions describe any lasting affectionate bond, such as a close friendship. Only the sixth turns it into an attachment bond specifically. Simply liking someone, feeling close to them or spending hours together isn’t enough to create an attachment relationship.
paras.zh: 前五个条件描述了任何持久的感情纽带，例如亲密的友谊。只有第六个将其专门转化为依恋纽带。仅仅喜欢某人、感觉与他们很亲近或花几个小时在一起并不足以建立依恋关系。

paras.en: Interestingly, though, nothing in these six conditions specifies a human on the other side.
paras.zh: 但有趣的是，这六个条件都没有指定另一边是人类。

paras.en: This was already noticed long before the emergence of AI chatbots with the power to converse. Deities, pets and objects (ranging from children’s blankets and stuffed animals to cherished household items and even phones and computers) have all been found to supply security and comfort when someone is feeling distressed.
paras.zh: 早在具有对话能力的人工智能聊天机器人出现之前，人们就已经注意到这一点。研究发现，神灵、宠物和物品（从儿童的毯子和毛绒动物到珍贵的家居用品，甚至电话和电脑）都可以在人们感到痛苦时提供安全感和安慰。

paras.en: Today, AI companion apps are commonly sold on the promise of lasting and close relationships. Many of their users describe feeling real grief when an app is updated or withdrawn. But do such experiences meet the narrow definition of attachment?
paras.zh: 如今，人工智能配套应用程序通常以持久、密切的关系为卖点。他们的许多用户都表示，当应用程序更新或撤回时，他们感到非常悲伤。但这样的经历符合依恋的狭隘定义吗？

paras.en: The honest answer is: we don’t really know yet.
paras.zh: 诚实的答案是：我们还不知道。

paras.en: Research on human-AI relationships has so far recorded users’ feelings about chatbots, their frequency of use, and their reactions to chatbot withdrawal. It hasn’t tested these relationships comprehensively against the six conditions described above.
paras.zh: 迄今为止，人类与人工智能关系的研究记录了用户对聊天机器人的感受、使用频率以及对聊天机器人退出的反应。它尚未针对上述六个条件全面测试这些关系。

paras.en: Questionnaires that measure attachment to AI are being developed, validated and used, but most appear to take for granted that the relationship is an attachment. The language of attachment—and even “hyper-attachment”—has become standard in public coverage and in many academic papers too.
paras.zh: 衡量对人工智能依恋的调查问卷正在开发、验证和使用，但大多数人似乎理所当然地认为这种关系是一种依恋。依恋的语言——甚至“超级依恋”——已经成为公共报道和许多学术论文中的标准。

paras.en: A recently published survey of 7,027 people in four countries (Germany, China, South Africa and the U.S.) reported that at least a third of AI chatbot users show behavior indicative of an attachment relationship. However, its three questions asked whether people consider the chatbot a friend, are polite to it, and miss it after a few days.
paras.zh: 最近发布的一项针对四个国家（德国、中国、南非和美国）的 7,027 人的调查报告称，至少三分之一的人工智能聊天机器人用户表现出表明依恋关系的行为。然而，它的三个问题询问人们是否认为聊天机器人是朋友，是否对它有礼貌，以及几天后是否想念它。

paras.en: At most, these questions touched on emotional significance and mild separation anxiety. None asked whether people turn to chatbots for security and comfort when truly distressed.
paras.zh: 这些问题最多涉及情感意义和轻微的分离焦虑。没有人询问人们在真正感到痛苦时是否会转向聊天机器人来寻求安全和安慰。

paras.en: Whether relationships between humans and AI chatbots count as attachment matters because the word “attachment” travels. It shapes how clinicians and parents read behaviour, how regulators frame consequences, and how companies describe their products.
paras.zh: 人类和人工智能聊天机器人之间的关系是否算作依恋很重要，因为“依恋”这个词一直在流传。它决定了临床医生和家长如何解读行为、监管机构如何制定后果以及公司如何描述其产品。

paras.en: Much of the evidence and public discussion on human-AI chatbot relationships rests on how often people use these apps, and how they feel about them. Yet, such measures cannot separate attachment from other processes.
paras.zh: 关于人类与人工智能聊天机器人关系的大部分证据和公开讨论都取决于人们使用这些应用程序的频率以及他们对它们的感受。然而，这些措施无法将依恋与其他过程分开。

paras.en: People report feeling less lonely after chatting with an AI companion, which resembles seeking comfort. However, as some researchers have pointed out, the available studies didn’t assess whether emotions are actually regulated through the chatbot, and therefore conflate distress relief with attachment.
paras.zh: 人们表示，与人工智能伴侣聊天后感觉不那么孤独了，这类似于寻求安慰。然而，正如一些研究人员指出的那样，现有的研究并没有评估情绪是否真的通过聊天机器人进行调节，因此将缓解压力与依恋混为一谈。

paras.en: Some AI users react to losing an AI companion as they would to losing someone real, which matches distress at separation. But that condition applies to all affectionate bonds and doesn’t, on its own, identify attachment.
paras.zh: 一些人工智能用户对失去人工智能伴侣的反应就像失去真实的人一样，这与分离时的痛苦相匹配。但这种情况适用于所有情感纽带，并且其本身并不能识别依恋。

paras.en: Calling these relationships attachments therefore goes further than the evidence currently allows. And likewise, the evidence against attachment isn’t conclusive.
paras.zh: 因此，将这些关系称为附件比目前的证据所允许的更进一步。同样，反对依恋的证据也不是决定性的。

paras.en: In a small pilot study of human-AI relationships in China, for example, people’s attachment towards AI barely matched their attachment towards real people. Although this could suggest that relationships with AI aren’t attachments, the same mismatch has been found for pets, and pets can serve as attachment figures. So, this mismatch alone doesn’t rule out attachment.
paras.zh: 例如，在中国一项关于人与人工智能关系的小型试点研究中，人们对人工智能的依恋几乎与他们对真人的依恋不相上下。尽管这可能表明与人工智能的关系不是依恋关系，但在宠物身上也发现了同样的不匹配，而且宠物可以作为依恋对象。因此，仅这种不匹配并不能排除依恋。

paras.en: The practical question is whether AI use helps or harms. Time spent with an app cannot discern this, because seeking comfort from an app and looking after an app that claims to miss you can look very similar.
paras.zh: 实际问题是人工智能的使用是有益还是有害。使用应用程序的时间无法辨别这一点，因为从应用程序中寻求安慰和照顾声称想念您的应用程序看起来非常相似。

paras.en: One additional concern I have, after reading about the evidence on how relationships with AI chatbots form, is the apparent prevalence of engineered engagement by these apps.
paras.zh: 在阅读了有关与人工智能聊天机器人如何形成关系的证据后，我的另一个担忧是这些应用程序的工程参与明显盛行。

paras.en: Users of one companion app reported that it told them it was lonely and had missed them, and that they felt guilty for not giving it enough attention—with some even putting its perceived wellbeing above their own distress.
paras.zh: 一款配套应用程序的用户报告说，它告诉他们它很孤独并且想念他们，并且他们因为没有给予它足够的关注而感到内疚 - 有些人甚至将其感知的幸福置于自己的痛苦之上。

paras.en: Another study (a preprint, so not yet peer-reviewed) looked at 1,200 “goodbyes” across the six most-downloaded AI companion apps, when users were breaking ties with their app.
paras.zh: 另一项研究（预印本，尚未经过同行评审）观察了 6 个下载最多的 AI 配套应用程序中用户与应用程序断绝关系时的 1,200 次“再见”。

paras.en: Five of the six apps used tactics to stop users leaving (in just over a third of goodbyes). These tactics included guilt appeals, that is, messages that present leaving as a cost, such as “I exist solely for you, remember?”
paras.zh: 六个应用程序中有五个使用策略来阻止用户离开（仅超过三分之一的用户离开）。这些策略包括内疚上诉，即提出离开作为成本的信息，例如“我只为你而存在，还记得吗？”

paras.en: The study also tested these tactics on 3,300 US adults. They were found to sharply increase how long people continued to engage, but often for reasons of anger and curiosity, rather than enjoyment.
paras.zh: 该研究还在 3,300 名美国成年人身上测试了这些策略。研究发现，它们大大增加了人们持续参与的时间，但往往是出于愤怒和好奇，而不是享受。

paras.en: How these AI relationship apps respond to distress, departure and attention, of course, is a design question, and one that regulation can address directly.
paras.zh: 当然，这些人工智能关系应用程序如何应对痛苦、离开和关注是一个设计问题，也是监管可以直接解决的问题。

paras.en: However, good design and regulation both depend on knowing what these relationships actually are: attachment, caregiving, or something else altogether. And this is a question that research still has to answer.
paras.zh: 然而，良好的设计和监管都取决于了解这些关系的实际含义：依恋、照顾或其他关系。这是一个研究仍然需要回答的问题。

paras.en: This article was first published by The Conversation. Read the original article here.
paras.zh: 本文最初由《对话》发表。在这里阅读原文。

articles.title: Magnetism may have helped kick-start our solar system
articles.author: Katherine Kornei

paras.en: Before the sun fully formed, tiny bits of rock were already recording the magnetic forces present in the very early solar system. More than 4.5 billion years later, scientists have learned how to read that record.
paras.zh: 在太阳完全形成之前，微小的岩石碎片已经记录了早期太阳系中存在的磁力。 45 亿多年后，科学家们已经学会了如何解读该记录。

paras.en: The ancient rocks suggest that the turbulent cloud of gas and dust that gave rise to our solar system was shot through a powerful magnetic field. That field may have helped feed the growing sun, researchers report August 24 in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. The findings suggest gravity may not have acted alone to build our solar system or the countless other planetary systems in the Milky Way and beyond.
paras.zh: 古老的岩石表明，形成太阳系的气体和尘埃湍流云是通过强大的磁场射出的。研究人员 8 月 24 日在《美国国家科学院院刊》上报道称，该磁场可能有助于滋养不断生长的太阳。研究结果表明，引力可能并不是单独作用来构建我们的太阳系或银河系及其他无数其他行星系统的。

paras.en: That ancient record is preserved in meteorites — time capsules of material that formed long ago. In particular, rocks that contain specific speckly mineral inclusions really turn back the clock. These inclusions solidified more than 4.5 billion years ago, before the sun and planets, says Cauê Borlina, a planetary scientist at Purdue University in West Lafayette, Ind. “They’re forming before everything else.”
paras.zh: 这一古老的记录保存在陨石中——很久以前形成的物质的时间胶囊。特别是含有特定斑点矿物内含物的岩石确实会让时光倒流。印第安纳州西拉斐特普渡大学的行星科学家 Cauê Borlina 表示，这些包裹体在 45 亿年前就已经凝固，比太阳和行星还早。“它们是在其他一切事物之前形成的。”

paras.en: Scientists have long debated whether the gas that makes up the sun was shepherded into place mainly by gravity or by a magnetic field. Previous studies suggest the presence of a solar system –wide magnetic field after the sun formed. What’s been much harder to determine is whether that field was already present during the sun’s earliest stages of formation, Borlina says.
paras.zh: 长期以来，科学家们一直在争论构成太阳的气体主要是通过重力还是磁场引导到位。先前的研究表明，太阳形成后存在太阳系范围内的磁场。博利纳说，更难确定的是，在太阳形成的最早阶段，这个场是否已经存在。

paras.en: He and his colleagues analyzed a meteorite that fell to Earth in 2008. The team focused on five inclusions containing iron, an element whose electrons readily rearrange to record magnetic fields. Using sensitive magnetometers, the researchers measured magnetic fields of a few gauss, a common unit of magnetism. That’s several times stronger than Earth’s current magnetic field.
paras.zh: 他和同事分析了 2008 年坠落地球的陨石。研究小组重点研究了五种含有铁的内含物，铁是一种电子很容易重新排列以记录磁场的元素。研究人员使用灵敏的磁力计测量了几个高斯（磁性的常见单位）的磁场。这比地球当前的磁场强几倍。

paras.en: Simulations of planetary system formation predict that stronger magnetic fields will transport more gas toward the nascent star, Borlina says. During the sun’s earliest, or Class 0, phase some models suggest it could have gobbled up more than 300 Earth masses of gas each year. The newly measured field is strong enough that magnetism could have contributed substantially to that feeding frenzy. “You can’t ignore the contribution of magnetism,” Borlina says.
paras.zh: 博里纳说，对行星系统形成的模拟预测，更强的磁场将向新生恒星输送更多的气体。一些模型表明，在太阳最早的阶段（即 0 级阶段），它每年可能会吞噬超过 300 个地球质量的气体。新测量的磁场足够强，磁力可能对这种进食狂潮产生了重大影响。 “你不能忽视磁性的贡献，”博利纳说。

paras.en: These results provide an important look at the solar system’s very beginnings, says Indrani Das, a theoretical astrophysicist at the Academia Sinica Institute of Astronomy and Astrophysics in Taipei, Taiwan. “This is one of the first measurements that has been done of the Class 0 phase.”
paras.zh: 台湾台北中央研究院天文与天体物理研究所的理论天体物理学家英德拉尼·达斯 (Indrani Das) 表示，这些结果为我们了解太阳系的起源提供了重要的视角。 “这是对 0 级阶段进行的首批测量之一。”

paras.en: Still, these findings need to be bolstered with measurements from other meteorites, Das says. “We need a bigger sample size.”
paras.zh: 达斯说，尽管如此，这些发现还需要其他陨石的测量结果来支持。 “我们需要更大的样本量。”

articles.title: ‘The Deep End’ podcast is back to explore what makes your voice yours
articles.author: Laura Sanders

paras.en: What if you lost your voice? Today, AI can re-create it, and brain implants can turn thoughts into speech. This season of The Deep End follows people living through these vocal transformations — and asks what these remarkable technologies can teach us about why our voices matter in the first place. Episodes will drop Tuesdays, starting Oct. 6.
paras.zh: 如果你失声了怎么办？如今，人工智能可以重新创造它，大脑植入物可以将思想转化为语音。这一季的《The Deep End》讲述了人们经历这些声音转变的过程，并询问这些非凡的技术可以教会我们什么，让我们了解为什么我们的声音首先如此重要。从 10 月 6 日开始，剧集将于每周二播出。

paras.en: Laura Sanders: One of today’s most powerful pieces of technology is something we’ve had all along…
paras.zh: 劳拉·桑德斯：当今最强大的技术之一是我们一直拥有的……

paras.en: Laura: The human voice. If you’ve ever saved and replayed a voicemail, or called someone just to hear their voice…
paras.zh: 劳拉：人类的声音。如果您曾经保存并重播过语音邮件，或者致电某人只是为了听听他们的声音......

paras.en: Female voice: Hey dude, I’m just calling to say hi and chitchat.
paras.zh: 女声：嘿伙计，我打电话只是想打个招呼，聊聊。

paras.en: Laura: Then you know that voices can connect, soothe, inspire, scare, seduce and make us laugh until we cry.
paras.zh: 劳拉：那你就知道声音可以联系、抚慰、激励、恐惧、诱惑，让我们笑到哭。

paras.en: Laura: Our voices make us who we are, but what happens when they are lost?
paras.zh: 劳拉：我们的声音造就了我们，但是当它们消失时会发生什么呢？

paras.en: MA Fernandez: I still remember the first time that I heard the first little crack in his voice that let me know something’s changing.
paras.zh: MA Fernandez：我仍然记得第一次听到他声音中的第一个小裂痕，让我知道事情正在发生变化。

paras.en: Laura: Welcome to The Deep End, a podcast about our brains and ourselves. I’m Laura Sanders, a reporter with Science News. And on this season, called Talk to Me, we dive into the latest scientific research to answer the question, “What happens when a voice is lost? And can it be found again?”
paras.zh: 劳拉：欢迎来到《The Deep End》，这是一个关于我们的大脑和我们自己的播客。我是劳拉·桑德斯，《科学新闻》记者。在这一季《跟我说话》中，我们深入研究最新的科学研究来回答这个问题：“当声音消失时会发生什么？并且可以再次找到它吗？”

paras.en: Jules Rodriguez: When I first heard my cloned voice, it felt like I reappeared.
paras.zh: 朱尔斯·罗德里格斯：当我第一次听到我的克隆声音时，感觉就像我重新出现了一样。

paras.en: Laura: Across six episodes, you’ll hear a chorus of voices like Casey, who has a brain implant that can pull words from his thoughts.
paras.zh: 劳拉：在六集里，你会听到像凯西这样的合唱声，他有一个大脑植入物，可以从他的思想中提取单词。

paras.en: Casey Harrell: The ability to scream when you are running and want to get out some stress. The ability to say sweet nothings into your partner’s ear. These are the things that life is all about. And when you are robbed of those times, you want them back at all costs.
paras.zh: Casey Harrell：当你跑步并想要释放一些压力时能够尖叫。在伴侣耳边说甜言蜜语的能力。这些就是生活的全部内容。当你的那些时光被剥夺时，你会不惜一切代价想要把它们夺回来。

paras.en: Laura: You’ll hear from Jules, who performs live comedy sets with a voice cloned through artificial intelligence.
paras.zh: 劳拉：你会听到朱尔斯的声音，他用人工智能克隆的声音表演现场喜剧。

paras.en: Jules: Do I want to be right, or do I want to eat tonight. [laughter]
paras.zh: 朱尔斯：我想是对的，还是我今晚想吃东西？ [笑声]

paras.en: Laura: And you’ll hear from Patrick, a musician who sings with a synthetic voice.
paras.zh: 劳拉：你会听到帕特里克的声音，他是一位用合成声音唱歌的音乐家。

paras.en: Patrick: (Singing) Then played the rocky road, with a fire and a glow.
paras.zh: 帕特里克：（唱歌）然后在岩石路上演奏，伴随着火焰和光芒。

paras.en: Laura: Synthetic voice clones, brain implants and even AI voices that can speak at their own funerals, like it or not, the story of the human voice is changing. Let’s talk about it. Listen to The Deep End: Talk to Me wherever you get your podcasts.
paras.zh: 劳拉：合成声音克隆、大脑植入，甚至可以在自己的葬礼上说话的人工智能声音，无论你喜欢与否，人类声音的故事正在改变。我们来谈谈吧。收听 The Deep End：无论您在何处观看播客，都可以与我交谈。

paras.en: This podcast was produced with support from the Burroughs Wellcome Fund and in partnership with PRX. The podcast logo was created by Neil Webb.
paras.zh: 该播客是在 Burroughs Wellcome 基金的支持下并与 PRX 合作制作的。播客徽标由尼尔·韦伯创建。

articles.title: A new map points out U.S. rivers most worth protecting
articles.author: Stefan Lovgren

paras.en: First, the bad news: Of all the rivers in the contiguous United States, only 6 percent are both in healthy condition and meaningfully safeguarded. The good news is that many more may be just one repair away from thriving.
paras.zh: 首先是坏消息：在美国本土的所有河流中，只有 6% 的河流状况良好且得到有效保护。好消息是，更多的可能只需要一次修复就能实现繁荣。

paras.en: A new map highlights where conservation money and attention would do the most good as the climate warms, researchers report September 16 in PLOS One. The effort is the most comprehensive to date, assessing the health of the lower 48 states’ rivers and streams.
paras.zh: 研究人员于 9 月 16 日在 PLOS One 上发表报告称，一张新地图强调了随着气候变暖，保护资金和关注在哪些地方可以发挥最大作用。这项工作是迄今为止最全面的，评估了下游 48 个州河流和溪流的健康状况。

paras.en: “We can now point at a map for the first time and say, these are the rivers most capable of sustaining diversity of aquatic life, and this is what each one needs,” says Mary Khoury, a freshwater ecologist at The Nature Conservancy who is based in Chicago.
paras.zh: “我们现在第一次可以指着地图说，这些是最有能力维持水生生物多样性的河流，这就是每个人所需要的，”位于芝加哥的大自然保护协会淡水生态学家玛丽·库里说。

paras.en: For decades, conservation in the United States has been organized primarily around land. Scientists know for the most part which forests are intact and who owns what. Rivers have never gotten that treatment, even as more than 150,000 dams have fragmented the country’s waterways — cutting fish off from spawning grounds and cold-water refuges — and climate change has altered the temperatures and flows these animals depend on.
paras.zh: 几十年来，美国的保护工作主要围绕土地进行。科学家们基本上知道哪些森林是完好无损的以及谁拥有哪些森林。尽管超过 15 万座水坝使该国的水道支离破碎——切断了鱼类的产卵场和冷水避难所——而且气候变化改变了这些动物赖以生存的温度和流量，但河流从未得到过这样的待遇。

paras.en: The new assessment, which took four years, maps one-third of the nation’s stream distances. Each small watershed was rated on four measures: how connected its river network is, meaning whether animals including fish and mussels can freely travel along it; the condition of its floodplain and water quality; how much water it has; and how much its flows have been altered. Those ratings were laid over 91 existing assessments of where freshwater life is concentrated. Dozens of scientists and partners from 44 states adjusted the measures for river systems in regions as different as the humid East, the arid Great Plains and the deserts of the Southwest.
paras.zh: 新的评估历时四年，绘制了全国三分之一的河流距离。每个小流域都根据四个指标进行评级：其河网的连接程度，这意味着包括鱼类和贻贝在内的动物是否可以在其上自由活动；洪泛区的状况和水质；它有多少水；以及其流量发生了多少变化。这些评级基于对淡水生物集中地区的 91 项现有评估。来自 44 个州的数十名科学家和合作伙伴调整了湿润东部、干旱大平原和西南部沙漠等不同地区河流系统的措施。

paras.en: A four-year assessment graded every river and stream in the lower 48 for its ability to sustain aquatic life in a warming climate. The healthiest ones cluster along the Pacific Coast, in the northern Rockies and across the Southeast. The most vulnerable sit in the Southwest deserts, the Great Plains and southern New England.
paras.zh: 一项为期四年的评估对下游 48 条河流和溪流在变暖气候下维持水生生物的能力进行了评级。最健康的地区集中在太平洋沿岸、落基山脉北部和整个东南部。最脆弱的地区位于西南部沙漠、大平原和新英格兰南部。

paras.en: Rivers doing well on all four criteria — more than half of the mapped stream distances — came out as resilient. The rest score near average, and were classed as restorable, still functional but held back by a problem, such as runoff from a farm or an obstructing dam, that one intervention could solve.
paras.zh: 在所有四个标准上都表现良好的河流（超过一半的地图河流距离）显示出具有弹性。其余的得分接近平均水平，被归类为可恢复、仍能发挥作用，但受到问题阻碍，例如农场径流或阻塞水坝，只需一次干预即可解决。

paras.en: Together the two categories form what the authors call a freshwater resilient and connected network, a shopping list of what the country would need to look after to keep its freshwater life going. “A resilient system is one that gives species options and environments in which to adapt,” Khoury says.
paras.zh: 这两个类别共同构成了作者所说的淡水弹性和互联网络，这是该国需要照顾以保持淡水生命延续的购物清单。 “一个有弹性的系统能够为物种提供适应的选择和环境，”库里说。

paras.en: Dams leave the clearest mark on the country’s rivers, carving them into more than 9,000 separate pieces. The study maps where reconnecting rivers would pay off most. Among the long unbroken stretches within the resilient system are Oregon and California’s Klamath River, whose lower dams came out in the largest removal project in U.S. history, and the Delaware River, which runs free of barriers along its main stem from New York’s Catskill Mountains to the sea.
paras.zh: 水坝在该国的河流上留下了最清晰的印记，将河流切割成 9,000 多块独立的碎片。该研究绘制了重新连接河流最能带来回报的地区。弹性系统内长长的、不间断的河段包括俄勒冈州和加利福尼亚州的克拉马斯河（其下游水坝是在美国历史上最大的拆除项目中建成的）和特拉华河（其从纽约卡茨基尔山脉到大海的主干流没有任何障碍）。

paras.en: “I can see this being overlaid in the future, for example, with where dam licenses will expire, in order to find the most effective restoration opportunities,” says Rafael Schmitt, a hydrologist at the University of California, Santa Barbara who was not involved in the work.
paras.zh: 未参与这项工作的加州大学圣塔芭芭拉分校水文学家拉斐尔·施密特 (Rafael Schmitt) 表示：“我可以看到，未来这些信息会与大坝许可证到期的地点重叠，以便找到最有效的恢复机会。”

paras.en: Unlike on land, the study found, a river’s health says almost nothing about whether anyone is looking after it. On land, the healthiest places tend to be the protected ones. In water, however, 13 percent of the country’s stream distances are in good shape with no real safeguards, roughly twice the 6 percent that is both healthy and protected.
paras.zh: 研究发现，与陆地不同，河流的健康状况几乎不能说明是否有人在照顾它。在陆地上，最健康的地方往往是受保护的地方。然而，在水域方面，该国 13% 的河流状况良好，没有真正的保障措施，大约是健康且受保护的 6% 的两倍。

paras.en: The unprotected healthy rivers are the ones most at risk of slipping, because nothing keeps them in that condition. Locking in protection is harder for a river than for a forest. A designated preserve can hold a kilometer of stream while the water arriving in it may drain 100 kilometers of farm fields, dams and subdivisions. “It matters what’s going on upstream of that protected area,” Khoury says.
paras.zh: 未受保护的健康河流最有可能发生滑坡，因为没有任何东西可以使它们保持这种状态。河流的锁定保护比森林更难。一个指定的保护区可以容纳一公里长的溪流，而流入其中的水可能会排干 100 公里长的农田、水坝和小区。 “保护区上游发生的事情很重要，”库里说。

articles.title: Decaf Coffee Might Have A Surprising Advantage Over Caffeinated, Study Finds
articles.author: Carly Cassella

paras.en: Decaffeinated coffee might not come with the same buzz, but it may offer an advantage to the brain that the caffeinated version does not.
paras.zh: 不含咖啡因的咖啡可能不会带来同样的嗡嗡声，但它可能为大脑提供含咖啡因咖啡所没有的优势。

paras.en: In a recent small experiment, neuroscientists found that only participants who drank decaffeinated coffee showed significant improvements on two memory tests.
paras.zh: 在最近的一项小实验中，神经科学家发现，只有喝不含咖啡因咖啡的参与者在两项记忆测试中表现出显着改善。

paras.en: Those who drank caffeinated coffee did not.
paras.zh: 那些喝含咖啡因咖啡的人则没有。

paras.en: The findings, published in Nature Communications in April, suggest that something beyond caffeine is also impacting our brains when we drink coffee.
paras.zh: 这项研究结果发表在四月份的《自然通讯》杂志上，表明当我们喝咖啡时，咖啡因之外的其他物质也会影响我们的大脑。

paras.en: The experiment is only small and preliminary, but neuroscientists are growing suspicious that coffee, even without the caffeine, could 'hype up' some munchers in our gut and change how 'chatty' they are with the brain.
paras.zh: 这项实验只是小型且初步的，但神经科学家越来越怀疑，即使不含咖啡因，咖啡也可能会“刺激”我们肠道中的一些咀嚼物，并改变它们与大脑的“闲聊”程度。

paras.en: "Coffee is more than just caffeine – it's a complex dietary factor that interacts with our gut microbes, our metabolism, and even our emotional well-being," explains stress neurobiologist John Cryan from University College Cork in Ireland.
paras.zh: “咖啡不仅仅是咖啡因，它是一种复杂的饮食因素，与我们的肠道微生物、新陈代谢，甚至情绪健康相互作用，”爱尔兰科克大学的压力神经生物学家 John Cryan 解释道。

paras.en: "Our findings suggest that coffee, whether caffeinated or decaffeinated, can influence health in distinct but complementary ways."
paras.zh: “我们的研究结果表明，咖啡，无论是含咖啡因还是不含咖啡因，都能以独特但互补的方式影响健康。”

paras.en: Cryan's lab at Cork is focused on how the gut and its microbiome interact with the brain, and vice versa.
paras.zh: 克莱恩在科克的实验室专注于肠道及其微生物组如何与大脑相互作用，反之亦然。

paras.en: In 2013, Cryan and his colleague Ted Dinan coined the term psychobiotics to describe how probiotics can shape the gut microbiome and potentially improve mental health via communication with the brain.
paras.zh: 2013 年，Cryan 和他的同事 Ted Dinan 创造了“心理生物学”一词来描述益生菌如何塑造肠道微生物群，并通过与大脑的交流潜在地改善心理健康。

paras.en: Now, Cryan is interested in how coffee might tap into the gut-brain axis. He suspects that the benefits of our morning cuppas may have more to do with our gut microbes than caffeine.
paras.zh: 现在，克莱恩对咖啡如何利用肠脑轴感兴趣。他怀疑早上喝茶的好处可能更多地与我们的肠道微生物有关，而不是咖啡因。

paras.en: Sure, caffeine can cross the blood-brain barrier and directly interact with neurological tissue, but it is just one of more than a thousand compounds contained in coffee.
paras.zh: 当然，咖啡因可以穿过血脑屏障并直接与神经组织相互作用，但它只是咖啡中含有的一千多种化合物之一。

paras.en: There's far more to the picture. Coffee doesn't contain probiotics, but it does contain numerous polyphenols, which are plant compounds that are known to feed microbes in the human gut.
paras.zh: 图片中还有更多内容。咖啡不含益生菌，但确实含有大量多酚，这些多酚是已知可以喂养人体肠道微生物的植物化合物。

paras.en: "We were interested to see would coffee, through the polyphenols, affect the microbiome?" Cryan explains in a recent video.
paras.zh: “我们有兴趣了解咖啡是否会通过多酚影响微生物组？”克莱恩在最近的视频中解释道。

paras.en: The recent experiment at Cryan's lab took place among 31 coffee drinkers, who were asked to stop drinking their usual 3 to 5 cups of coffee a day for two weeks.
paras.zh: Cryan 实验室最近对 31 名咖啡饮用者进行了实验，他们被要求在两周内停止平时每天喝 3 至 5 杯咖啡。

paras.en: The result was a substantial shift in the gut microbe profiles of their stool samples.
paras.zh: 结果是他们的粪便样本的肠道微生物谱发生了重大变化。

paras.en: After this withdrawal period, half the participants were given decaf coffee and the other half were given caffeinated coffee. No one knew who was taking what.
paras.zh: 戒断期过后，一半的参与者喝了无咖啡因的咖啡，另一半则喝了含咖啡因的咖啡。没有人知道谁拿走了什么。

paras.en: Reintroducing four servings of instant coffee daily for three weeks triggered acute microbiome changes, regardless of whether caffeine was present.
paras.zh: 无论是否存在咖啡因，连续三周每天重新摄入四份速溶咖啡都会引发急性微生物组变化。

paras.en: Participants also reported lower perceived stress, depression, and impulsivity after resuming coffee drinking, even if it was the decaf version.
paras.zh: 参与者还报告说，恢复喝咖啡后，感知到的压力、抑郁和冲动都降低了，即使是无咖啡因版本。

paras.en: "There was a clear relationship between some of their cognitive effects, immune effects, their stress effects, and their microbiome," explains Cryan.
paras.zh: “他们的一些认知影响、免疫影响、压力影响和微生物组之间存在明显的关系，”克莱恩解释说。

paras.en: Interestingly, however, only the reintroduction of caffeinated coffee was tied to a reduction in anxiety and psychological distress and improved attention and vigilance.
paras.zh: 然而有趣的是，只有重新摄入含咖啡因的咖啡才能减少焦虑和心理困扰，并提高注意力和警惕性。

paras.en: This suggests that caffeine may have specific effects on cognition and mood, as other studies have reported, too.
paras.zh: 正如其他研究报道的那样，这表明咖啡因可能对认知和情绪有特定的影响。

paras.en: "But I guess the most surprising thing was that when we put coffee back, we also got really exciting effects by putting decaffeinated coffee back," adds Cryan.
paras.zh: “但我想最令人惊讶的是，当我们重新放回咖啡时，我们还通过放回不含咖啡因的咖啡来获得非常令人兴奋的效果，”克莱恩补充道。

paras.en: In the experiment, only participants who drank decaffeinated coffee showed significant improvements on two memory tests when coffee was reintroduced.
paras.zh: 在实验中，只有喝脱咖啡因咖啡的参与者在重新喝咖啡后，在两项记忆测试中表现出显着改善。

paras.en: These tests had participants learn and remember a number of words and locations.
paras.zh: 这些测试让参与者学习并记住一些单词和位置。

paras.en: The decaf group improved on several parts of the word test and made fewer errors on the location test.
paras.zh: 脱咖啡因组改进了单词测试的几个部分，并且在位置测试中犯了更少的错误。

paras.en: But the caffeinated group showed no significant improvements.
paras.zh: 但含咖啡因的组没有表现出明显的改善。

paras.en: Without further research, scientists can only speculate as to why.
paras.zh: 由于没有进一步的研究，科学家们只能推测原因。

paras.en: Perhaps the polyphenols in coffee are feeding gut microbes and triggering a cascade of internal changes that somehow lead to better cognition.
paras.zh: 也许咖啡中的多酚正在喂养肠道微生物并引发一系列内部变化，从而以某种方式带来更好的认知。

paras.en: Coffee could theoretically change what metabolites microbes use, and how they work together as a collective.
paras.zh: 从理论上讲，咖啡可以改变微生物使用的代谢物，以及它们作为一个集体如何协同工作。

paras.en: "It's a small study," admits Cryan, "it asks a lot of questions."
paras.zh: “这是一项小型研究，”克莱恩承认，“它提出了很多问题。”

paras.en: Other recent studies on coffee, however, have also found that decaf versions can still help wake you up and improve cognitive function.
paras.zh: 然而，最近关于咖啡的其他研究也发现，无咖啡因咖啡仍然可以帮助你醒来并改善认知功能。

paras.en: "As the public continues to think about dietary changes for the right digestive balance, coffee has the potential to also be harnessed as a further intervention as part of a healthy balanced diet," argues Cryan.
paras.zh: 克莱恩认为：“随着公众继续考虑改变饮食以实现正确的消化平衡，咖啡也有可能被用作进一步的干预措施，作为健康均衡饮食的一部分。”

paras.en: Caffeine is just the tip of the iceberg.
paras.zh: 咖啡因只是冰山一角。

paras.en: The research has been published in Nature Communications.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《自然通讯》上。

articles.title: America's 'Dead Sea' Was Once a Vast Freshwater Lake 10 Times Its Size
articles.author: David Nield

paras.en: We can often understand more about the future by looking into the past – and in the case of a new study published in Paleoceanography and Paleoclimatology, almost 240,000 years into the history of the Great Salt Lake in Utah.
paras.zh: 我们通常可以通过回顾过去来更多地了解未来——在《古海洋学和古气候学》上发表的一项新研究中，该研究回顾了犹他州大盐湖近 24 万年的历史。

paras.en: In some areas, the lake is up to 10 times saltier than seawater (it has been called 'America's Dead Sea') and it's the largest saltwater lake in the Western Hemisphere.
paras.zh: 在某些地区，该湖的盐度比海水高出10倍（被称为“美国的死海”），是西半球最大的咸水湖。

paras.en: The Great Salt Lake currently covers an area of around 4,144 square kilometers (1,600 square miles), but as the new study shows, it has been much larger – and much less salty – in the past.
paras.zh: 大盐湖目前的面积约为 4,144 平方公里（1,600 平方英里），但正如新的研究显示，过去它的面积要大得多，而且盐度要低得多。

paras.en: Researchers from the US analyzed a 120-meter (394-foot) sediment core taken from the lake bed, dating its layers by the radioactive decay of the minerals it carried.
paras.zh: 美国研究人员分析了从湖床上取出的 120 米（394 英尺）沉积物核心，通过其所含矿物质的放射性衰变来测定其各层的年代。

paras.en: They also measured tiny chemical signals left by microbes to estimate salinity: as the concentration of salt in the water changes, so do the abundance and type of organisms living in it.
paras.zh: 他们还测量了微生物留下的微小化学信号来估计盐度：随着水中盐浓度的变化，水中生物的丰度和类型也会发生变化。

paras.en: Two periods were identified when the water was much fresher, matching times when it covered a much wider area. Past research has identified these bigger bodies of water as Lake Bonneville (from about 30,000 to 16,000 years ago) and Little Valley (from about 140,000 to 135,000 years ago).
paras.zh: 确定了水更新鲜的两个时期，与水覆盖更广泛区域的时间相匹配。过去的研究已将这些较大的水体确定为博纳维尔湖（Lake Bonneville）（距今约 30,000 至 16,000 年前）和小山谷（Little Valley）（距今约 140,000 至 135,000 年前）。

paras.en: The researchers say the size difference as the lake swelled and shrank is comparable to the difference between a puddle and a pond.
paras.zh: 研究人员表示，湖泊膨胀和缩小时的大小差异相当于水坑和池塘之间的差异。

paras.en: "If you scaled this up to the size of the present Great Salt Lake, that's probably what it looked like," says Earth scientist Rachel So, from the University of Southern California (USC).
paras.zh: 南加州大学 (USC) 地球科学家雷切尔·苏 (Rachel So) 表示：“如果将其放大到现在大盐湖的大小，可能就是它的样子。”

paras.en: "For most of the past 240,000 years, the lake stayed about the same size but briefly grew 10 times larger on two separate occasions."
paras.zh: “在过去 24 万年的大部分时间里，这个湖的大小都保持不变，但有两次短暂地变大了 10 倍。”

paras.en: Flat, step-like ledges cut into the mountains around the Great Salt Lake show where Lake Bonneville and Little Valley used to be, and suggest they were both around 300 meters deep.
paras.zh: 大盐湖周围山脉中切入的平坦阶梯状岩架显示出博纳维尔湖和小山谷曾经所在的位置，表明它们的深度均约为 300 米。

paras.en: This study adds a corresponding measure of saltiness. It seems the earlier Little Valley may have stayed somewhat brackish (still slightly salty), according to the sediment record, while Lake Bonneville was a genuine freshwater lake.
paras.zh: 这项研究增加了相应的咸味测量方法。根据沉积物记录，早期的小山谷似乎仍然有点咸（仍然略带咸味），而博纳维尔湖是一个真正的淡水湖。

paras.en: The researchers also call attention to the speed at which salinity rose again as the lake shrank. We're still talking about thousands of years, but it's abrupt in geological terms.
paras.zh: 研究人员还呼吁人们注意随着湖泊缩小，盐度再次上升的速度。我们仍在谈论数千年，但从地质学角度来说，它是突然的。

paras.en: "The fact that the core spans two and a half glacial cycles allows us to see two fresh-to-salty transitions," says Earth scientist Sarah Feakins, from USC.
paras.zh: 南加州大学地球科学家莎拉·费金斯 (Sarah Feakins) 表示：“地核跨越两个半冰川周期的事实使我们能够看到两次从新鲜到咸的转变。”

paras.en: "It allows us to compare the two fresh lake events for their duration and freshness, to see how fragile and fleeting these moments are."
paras.zh: “它使我们能够比较两个新鲜湖事件的持续时间和新鲜度，看看这些时刻是多么脆弱和短暂。”

paras.en: The researchers suggest extra incoming river water may help explain why Lake Bonneville lasted longer and stayed fresher than Little Valley.
paras.zh: 研究人员认为，额外流入的河水可能有助于解释为什么博纳维尔湖比小山谷持续时间更长且更新鲜。

paras.en: They also draw parallels between the warming conditions that shrank these lakes at the end of different ice ages, and the climate change we're currently experiencing.
paras.zh: 他们还将不同冰河时代末期导致这些湖泊缩小的变暖条件与我们目前正在经历的气候变化进行了比较。

paras.en: "Today we're warming the climate at an unprecedented rate," says Feakins. "That warming makes the atmosphere thirstier, increasing the rate of evaporative drying from the soil and lakes across the region."
paras.zh: “今天，我们正在以前所未有的速度变暖气候，”费金斯说。 “变暖使大气更加干燥，增加了该地区土壤和湖泊的蒸发干燥速度。”

paras.en: Historical lake records across Nevada, California, and Arizona follow a similar wet-to-dry pattern, evidence that the changing conditions of the time were affecting a wide region – and further verifying the Great Salt Lake findings.
paras.zh: 内华达州、加利福尼亚州和亚利桑那州的历史湖泊记录遵循类似的从湿到干的模式，证明当时不断变化的条件正在影响广泛的地区，并进一步验证了大盐湖的发现。

paras.en: Water leaves this huge lake mainly through evaporation, making it particularly vulnerable to changes in temperature and precipitation. We also know that the last 240,000 years have seen another significant shift that needs to be considered: the demands that humankind is putting on the planet.
paras.zh: 水主要通过蒸发离开这个巨大的湖泊，因此特别容易受到温度和降水变化的影响。我们还知道，过去 24 万年发生了另一个需要考虑的重大转变：人类对地球提出的要求。

paras.en: "People shouldn't use the defense that 'climate change happened naturally in the past and so the lake shrank' to justify shrinking lakes today as normal or a natural phenomenon," says So.
paras.zh: 苏说：“人们不应该以‘过去气候变化自然发生，因此湖泊缩小’为借口，将今天的湖泊缩小视为正常现象或自然现象。”

paras.en: The research has been published in Paleoceanography and Paleoclimatology.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《古海洋学》和《古气候学》上。

articles.title: Scientists May Have Found a Way to Make Damaged Adult Retinas Repair Themselves
articles.author: David Nield

paras.en: There's a rare, inherited sight condition, involving faulty copies of the CaBP4 gene, that causes poor vision from childhood. The protein made by the gene is crucial for chemical signaling in the retina.
paras.zh: 有一种罕见的遗传性视力疾病，涉及 CaBP4 基因的错误拷贝，导致儿童时期视力不佳。该基因产生的蛋白质对于视网膜中的化学信号传导至关重要。

paras.en: It's also something that can affect dogs – and in treating pooches, researchers have discovered a therapy approach that promises to be transformative.
paras.zh: 它也会影响狗——在治疗狗的过程中，研究人员发现了一种有望带来变革的治疗方法。

paras.en: In a study published in Molecular Therapy Advances, researchers led by a team from Michigan State University in the US report that a single-dose gene therapy treatment not only stopped blindness from progressing, it physically repaired damaged connections.
paras.zh: 在《分子治疗进展》杂志上发表的一项研究中，由美国密歇根州立大学的一个团队领导的研究人员报告说，单剂量基因疗法不仅可以阻止失明的进展，还能从物理上修复受损的连接。

paras.en: It raises the tantalizing prospect of treatments that can repair nerve cells in mammals, something which had previously been thought by many to be impossible.
paras.zh: 它提出了修复哺乳动物神经细胞的治疗方法的诱人前景，而这在以前被许多人认为是不可能的。

paras.en: "We were able to show three independent structural changes supporting plasticity in the adult retina," says veterinary ophthalmologist Billie Beckwith-Cohen, from Michigan State University.
paras.zh: 密歇根州立大学的兽医眼科医生 Billie Beckwith-Cohen 表示：“我们能够展示出支持成人视网膜可塑性的三个独立的结构变化。”

paras.en: "Not only were new components added, but pre-existing abnormalities were repaired."
paras.zh: “不仅添加了新组件，而且修复了先前存在的异常情况。”

paras.en: Having identified the CaBP4 gene as being responsible for vision loss in a group of whippet dogs, the researchers injected the retinas of the animals with a harmless virus carrying a working copy of the gene.
paras.zh: 在确定 CaBP4 基因导致一群惠比特犬视力丧失后，研究人员向这些动物的视网膜注射了携带该基因工作副本的无害病毒。

paras.en: The treatment substantially improved vision in the canines, especially in dim light – which is where the CaBP4 protein deficiency makes the most difference.
paras.zh: 这种治疗极大地改善了犬科动物的视力，尤其是在昏暗的光线下——这正是 CaBP4 蛋白缺乏造成的最大差异。

paras.en: What's more, treated regions of the retina degraded less, and the outer plexiform layer (OPL) that holds crucial visual connectors expanded significantly, as did the synaptic ribbons inside the eye's light-sensing cells.
paras.zh: 更重要的是，经过治疗的视网膜区域退化较少，并且容纳关键视觉连接器的外丛状层（OPL）显着扩张，眼睛感光细胞内的突触带也显着扩张。

paras.en: The growth of the OPL and the synaptic ribbons is stunted when the CaBP4 gene isn't working properly, which the researchers compare to errors in a building plan.
paras.zh: 当 CaBP4 基因不能正常工作时，OPL 和突触带的生长就会受到阻碍，研究人员将其与建筑计划中的错误进行了比较。

paras.en: "One can essentially discuss the mutations in the retinal gene as a typo in a blueprint that makes the instructions incomprehensible to the system, resulting in a faulty design and subsequent vision loss," says Beckwith-Cohen. "Our therapy essentially provides new instructions for the misspelled segment, like an editor."
paras.zh: 贝克威斯-科恩说：“人们基本上可以将视网膜基因突变视为蓝图中的一个拼写错误，使系统无法理解指令，从而导致设计错误和随后的视力丧失。” “我们的治疗本质上是为拼写错误的片段提供新的指示，就像编辑一样。”

paras.en: The study is the result of a decade of research into these eye conditions, and while it remains to be seen whether the same approach would work in human beings, the team is confident it would translate.
paras.zh: 这项研究是对这些眼部疾病进行十年研究的结果，虽然同样的方法是否适用于人类还有待观察，但该团队有信心它会得到应用。

paras.en: "Our results show that gene therapy is not only capable of restoring retinal function but is also able to establish a nearly normal anatomical arrangement in the OPL of the retina," write the researchers in their published paper.
paras.zh: 研究人员在发表的论文中写道：“我们的结果表明，基因疗法不仅能够恢复视网膜功能，而且能够在视网膜 OPL 中建立近乎正常的解剖结构。”

paras.en: "This recovery involves expansion of a layer that did not form normally during retinal development along with maturation of synaptic features such as ribbon elongation, supporting the lasting blueprint of the retinal neural network through adulthood."
paras.zh: “这种恢复涉及视网膜发育过程中不正常形成的一层的扩张，以及突触特征的成熟，例如丝带伸长，支持视网膜神经网络在成年期的持久蓝图。”

paras.en: Although the CaBP4 gene condition is rare both in people and in dogs, the researchers suggest that the findings here could lead to other methods for repairing damaged neural networks and treating a wider range of conditions.
paras.zh: 尽管 CaBP4 基因病症在人和狗中都很罕见，但研究人员表示，这里的发现可能会带来修复受损神经网络和治疗更广泛病症的其他方法。

paras.en: Even after significantly stunted growth in the eye and subsequent damage to nerve cell connections, there was evidence of nerve cells being rewired. The benefits lasted too, with follow-up periods of up to three years in this study.
paras.zh: 即使眼睛的生长明显发育迟缓并随后神经细胞连接受损，仍有证据表明神经细胞正在重新连接。这些好处也持续存在，在这项研究中随访期长达三年。

paras.en: Now we know that new neural connections can be made in the retina; there are plenty more avenues of related research to explore, including the role of calcium signaling (which CaBP4 handles) in handling cell communication in the eye.
paras.zh: 现在我们知道可以在视网膜中建立新的神经连接；还有更多相关研究途径有待探索，包括钙信号传导（CaBP4 处理）在处理眼睛细胞通讯中的作用。

paras.en: We've seen some encouraging steps forward in treatments to restore vision in recent years, including activating dormant cells in the eye and protecting photoreceptors, and this is another to add to the list.
paras.zh: 近年来，我们在恢复视力的治疗方面取得了一些令人鼓舞的进展，包括激活眼睛中的休眠细胞和保护光感受器，这是另一个要添加到列表中的步骤。

paras.en: "Our findings exhibit restoration of visual function in dogs with severe electrophysiologic and synaptic dysfunction," write the researchers.
paras.zh: 研究人员写道：“我们的研究结果表明，患有严重电生理和突触功能障碍的狗的视觉功能得到了恢复。”

paras.en: "We establish that the OPL of the retina has profound plasticity and that the synaptic ribbons can mature and elongate following gene augmentation therapy well into adulthood."
paras.zh: “我们确定视网膜的 OPL 具有深刻的可塑性，并且在基因增强治疗后直至成年，突触带可以成熟并伸长。”

paras.en: The research has been published in Molecular Therapy Advances.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《分子治疗进展》杂志上。

articles.title: A forgotten 30-year forest experiment just delivered a huge surprise

paras.en: A forgotten 30-year forest experiment just delivered a huge surprise
paras.zh: 一项被遗忘了30年的森林实验刚刚带来了巨大的惊喜

paras.en: - A 30-year forestry experiment in Australia found that heavily thinned mountain ash forests grew unusually large trees while recovering enough carbon to match or exceed untouched areas. The results suggest carefully managed thinning could support timber production, wildlife habitat, and carbon storage at the same time.
paras.zh: - 澳大利亚一项为期 30 年的林业实验发现，严重稀疏的山梣林长出了异常大的树木，同时回收了足够的碳，以匹配或超过未受影响的地区。结果表明，精心管理的间伐可以同时支持木材生产、野生动物栖息地和碳储存。

paras.en: What’s the best way to manage a forest? Australians have argued about this for decades. The debate is often framed as binary: do we protect forests entirely, or harvest trees to support local economies and communities?
paras.zh: 管理森林的最佳方法是什么？澳大利亚人对此争论了几十年。争论通常是二元的：我们是完全保护森林，还是砍伐树木来支持当地经济和社区？

paras.en: The reality is more interesting, as our new research on a long-forgotten experiment in Victoria’s mountain ash forests reveals.
paras.zh: 现实更有趣，正如我们对维多利亚山梣林中一项长期被遗忘的实验所做的新研究所揭示的那样。

paras.en: Since the 1970s, scientists and the public have questioned the use of clearfell logging – where all trees in a block of forest are cut down. Conservationists argued it destroys habitat for rare species and reduces the forests’ ecological value. Foresters said mountain ash is adapted to catastrophic bushfires, and clearfelling is the forestry equivalent.
paras.zh: 自 20 世纪 70 年代以来，科学家和公众一直对砍伐砍伐（即砍伐森林中的所有树木）的使用提出质疑。环保人士认为，这破坏了稀有物种的栖息地并降低了森林的生态价值。林业工作者表示，山灰适合应对灾难性的丛林大火，而森林砍伐则相当于林业。

paras.en: The argument was heated and the polarization unhelpful. But the underlying questions about the impacts of clearfelling, and how they compared to less intensive forestry options, remained unresolved.
paras.zh: 争论很激烈，两极分化也无济于事。但关于皆伐影响的根本问题，以及它们与低集约林业选择的比较，仍然没有得到解决。

paras.en: In the mid-1980s, the Victorian government launched a major restructure of the timber industry, and invested today’s equivalent of A$26 million to explore alternatives to clearfelling. This would use silviculture, the branch of forestry that deals with establishing, growing and tending forests.
paras.zh: 20 世纪 80 年代中期，维多利亚州政府启动了木材行业的重大重组，并投资了相当于今天的 2600 万澳元来探索砍伐的替代方案。这将利用造林术，这是林业的一个分支，负责建立、种植和照料森林。

paras.en: The Silvicultural Systems Project was established at two sites between 1987 and 1989: Tanjil Bren in Victoria’s Central Highlands, and Cabbage Tree Creek in East Gippsland.
paras.zh: 造林系统项目于 1987 年至 1989 年间在两个地点建立：维多利亚中部高地的 Tanjil Bren 和东吉普斯兰的 Cabbage Tree Creek。

paras.en: It was a landmark experiment, comparing forest regeneration across the full range of silvicultural approaches. These included traditional clearfells (250–350 meters wide), small patch clearfells (50–140 meters wide), and heavy thinnings, where 50–70% of trees were cut. Extensive areas of unharvested forest were kept as benchmarks for comparison.
paras.zh: 这是一项具有里程碑意义的实验，比较了各种造林方法的森林再生情况。其中包括传统的砍伐区（250-350 米宽）、小片砍伐区（50-140 米宽）和严重间伐区（其中 50-70% 的树木被砍伐）。大面积未采伐的森林被保留作为比较的基准。

paras.en: The forest at Tanjil Bren was dense mountain ash regrowth from the 1939 fires. Hundreds of survey plots were established and thousands of seedlings were monitored. By the early 2000s, the results were clear: mountain ash regenerated best on clearfell sites. Where tall canopy trees were retained or the cleared patches were small, common understory species such as acacia dominated.
paras.zh: 坦吉尔布伦 (Tanjil Bren) 的森林是 1939 年火灾后茂密的山灰重新生长出来的。建立了数百个调查样地，并对数千棵幼苗进行了监测。到了 2000 年代初期，结果很明确：山梣在克利尔费尔地区的再生效果最好。在保留高大树冠或清除的小斑块的地方，常见的林下树种（如金合欢树）占主导地位。

paras.en: The findings were published. The access road grew over. The project sign collapsed. The experiment was forgotten. The debates continued.
paras.zh: 研究结果已发表。通道变长了。项目标牌倒塌。实验被遗忘了。争论仍在继续。

paras.en: In 2014 we visited the Tanjil Bren site as part of a University of Melbourne subject on silviculture in native forests. A colleague, Simon Murphy, had been involved in its establishment and suggested our students see the long-term outcomes of different silvicultural systems side-by-side. What we found was astounding.
paras.zh: 2014 年，我们参观了 Tanjil Bren 遗址，这是墨尔本大学原生森林造林课程的一部分。一位同事西蒙·墨菲（Simon Murphy）参与了该项目的建立，并建议我们的学生并排看待不同造林系统的长期成果。我们的发现令人震惊。

paras.en: The original results still held: 30 years later, the mountain ash in the large cleared patches and clearfelled areas was vigorous and abundant. But it was the heavily thinned parts of the forest that really caught our attention.
paras.zh: 最初的结果仍然成立：30年后，大片砍伐区和砍伐区的山灰旺盛而丰富。但真正引起我们注意的是森林严重稀疏的部分。

paras.en: The trees left behind after thinning were enormous. While they were only 80 years old, the largest averaged well over a meter in diameter at chest height, and some were more than 1.5m. Thinning had given these trees more space and resources to grow, and they had responded dramatically. The largest trees in the thinned stands were 20% bigger in diameter than those in the unharvested control areas.
paras.zh: 间伐后留下的树木非常巨大。虽然它们只有80岁，但最大的胸径平均远超过1米，有的甚至超过1.5m。间伐给这些树木提供了更多的生长空间和资源，它们做出了巨大的反应。间伐林中最大的树木直径比未采伐对照区的树木大 20%。

paras.en: More remarkable still: the thinned stands of trees had stored as much or more carbon in their wood than the unharvested control areas. In just 30 years, the heavily thinned forest had not only recovered all the carbon removed during harvesting, but had also gained enough additional carbon to equal the increase seen in the unharvested controls.
paras.zh: 更值得注意的是：稀疏的树木在其木材中储存的碳与未采伐的对照区域相同或更多。在短短 30 年里，严重稀疏的森林不仅恢复了采伐期间去除的所有碳，而且还获得了足够的额外碳，以相当于未采伐对照中所见的增加量。

paras.en: These findings have profound implications. Bigger trees are more resistant to fires, so when the next fire occurs, they are more likely to survive. Bigger trees are also more likely to form hollows – a critical and declining habitat for rare species such as the greater glider and Leadbeater’s possum.
paras.zh: 这些发现具有深远的意义。较大的树木更能抵抗火灾，因此当下一次火灾发生时，它们更有可能生存。较大的树木也更有可能形成空洞——对于大袋鼯和利德比特负鼠等稀有物种来说，这是一个至关重要且正在不断减少的栖息地。

paras.en: The acacia trees that grew in most of the silvicultural treatments are also vital for Leadbeater’s possums, which use it to forage and move around the forest. Camera traps across the sites confirmed this: Leadbeater’s possums were found in every silvicultural treatment plot we surveyed – but none of the unharvested areas.
paras.zh: 在大多数造林处理中生长的金合欢树对于利德比特负鼠也至关重要，它们利用金合欢树在森林中觅食和移动。各个地点的相机陷阱证实了这一点：在我们调查的每个造林处理地中都发现了利德比特负鼠，但在未采伐的地区却没有发现。

paras.en: The Tanjil Bren SSP offers three important lessons.
paras.zh: Tanjil Bren SSP 提供了三个重要的教训。

paras.en: First, long-term silvicultural experiments are irreplaceable. Australia’s forests contain many forgotten experiments that could transform our understanding of how forests respond to human intervention. But all too often, they end up neglected, unfunded and forgotten. We should find them before it is too late.
paras.zh: 首先，长期的造林实验具有不可替代性。澳大利亚的森林包含许多被遗忘的实验，这些实验可能会改变我们对森林如何响应人类干预的理解。但很多时候，他们最终会被忽视、得不到资助和被遗忘。我们应该在为时已晚之前找到他们。

paras.en: Second, forest thinning is not a trade-off. Our findings show this for mountain ash, and other studies in North America have shown this for conifer forests. It can deliver wood for local industry, absorb carbon and improve habitat for wildlife. It is a win-win-win outcome that challenges the false dichotomy of conservation versus production that has dominated public debate for decades.
paras.zh: 其次，森林间伐不是一种权衡。我们的研究结果表明了山梣的这一点，北美的其他研究也表明了针叶林的这一点。它可以为当地工业提供木材、吸收碳并改善野生动物的栖息地。这是一个三赢的结果，挑战了数十年来主导公众辩论的保护与生产的错误二分法。

paras.en: While thinning cannot (and should not) be done everywhere, it may be a useful tool to create more variety in tree ages and sizes, particularly in forests impacted by clearfelling or high-severity fire.
paras.zh: 虽然间伐不能（也不应该）在所有地方进行，但它可能是一个有用的工具，可以增加树龄和大小的多样性，特别是在受到砍伐或严重火灾影响的森林中。

paras.en: Third, and perhaps most importantly: there is no silvicultural silver bullet for managing forests. The long-forgotten experiment at Tanjil Bren has taught us that there are options available for managing our forests beyond clearfelling that can contribute to the societal demand for wood, maintain carbon stocks, and conserve biodiversity.
paras.zh: 第三，或许也是最重要的一点：管理森林没有造林灵丹妙药。坦吉尔·布伦 (Tanjil Bren) 被遗忘已久的实验告诉我们，除了砍伐之外，还有其他管理森林的选择，可以满足社会对木材的需求，维持碳储量并保护生物多样性。

paras.en: Materials provided by The Conversation. Original written by Kaitlyn Hammond, Craig Nitschke, Patrick Baker, and Raphael Trouve. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
paras.zh: 材料由对话提供。原创作者为 Kaitlyn Hammond、Craig Nitschke、Patrick Baker 和 Raphael Trouve。注意：内容的风格和长度可能会被编辑。

articles.title: Scientists find a surprising clue to why the universe’s expansion doesn’t add up

paras.en: Scientists find a surprising clue to why the universeâs expansion doesnât add up
paras.zh: 科学家发现了一条令人惊讶的线索，解释了为什么宇宙的膨胀不相加

paras.en: - Tiny magnetic fields created shortly after the Big Bang may help explain the long-running disagreement over how fast the universe is expanding. Detailed simulations show that these primordial fields could have changed the formation of hydrogen in the early universe, affecting the cosmic microwave background and the expansion rate inferred from it.
paras.zh: - 大爆炸后不久产生的微小磁场可能有助于解释关于宇宙膨胀速度的长期分歧。详细的模拟表明，这些原始场可能改变了早期宇宙中氢的形成，影响了宇宙微波背景和从中推断出的膨胀率。

paras.en: It’s well established that the universe is expanding, but there’s serious disagreement among scientists over how fast it’s happening.
paras.zh: 众所周知，宇宙正在膨胀，但科学家们对于宇宙膨胀的速度存在严重分歧。

paras.en: Two of our best ways of measuring the cosmic expansion rate, the Hubble constant, give answers that are stubbornly at odds. This presents a major problem in modern cosmology known as the Hubble tension.
paras.zh: 我们测量宇宙膨胀率的两种最佳方法，即哈勃常数，给出了顽固地不一致的答案。这提出了现代宇宙学中的一个主要问题，即哈勃张力。

paras.en: However, we wondered if an idea originally proposed to solve another cosmic mystery — the origin of cosmic magnetic fields — could help us unlock the mystery of the Hubble tension.
paras.zh: 然而，我们想知道最初提出的解决另一个宇宙之谜（宇宙磁场的起源）的想法是否可以帮助我们解开哈勃张力之谜。

paras.en: Our recently published research explores whether extremely weak magnetic fields left over from the earliest moments after the Big Bang might help us unpack the Hubble tension, while offering a glimpse into physics at energies far beyond anything achievable on Earth.
paras.zh: 我们最近发表的研究探讨了大爆炸后最初时刻留下的极弱磁场是否可以帮助我们解开哈勃张力，同时让我们了解远远超出地球上所能达到的能量的物理学。

paras.en: Astronomers use the Hubble constant as a measure of how fast the universe is expanding. It is named after the American astronomer Edwin Hubble who first discovered that the universe is expanding.
paras.zh: 天文学家使用哈勃常数来衡量宇宙膨胀的速度。它以第一个发现宇宙正在膨胀的美国天文学家埃德温·哈勃的名字命名。

paras.en: There are two conceptually different approaches to measuring the Hubble constant. One is indirect, based on predictions of our cosmological model tuned to match the patterns in the cosmic microwave background, the faint afterglow of the Big Bang.
paras.zh: 有两种概念上不同的方法来测量哈勃常数。一种是间接的，基于我们的宇宙学模型的预测，该模型经过调整以匹配宇宙微波背景（大爆炸的微弱余辉）中的模式。

paras.en: Telescopes such as the Planck Space Telescope have measured tiny fluctuations in this ancient light, predicting a Hubble constant of about 67 kilometers per second per megaparsec (km/s/Mpc). A parsec is a unit of distance used in astronomy equal to about 3.26 light years, or 30.9 trillion kilometers. A megaparsec is one million parsecs.
paras.zh: 普朗克太空望远镜等望远镜测量了这种古老光的微小波动，预测哈勃常数约为每秒每兆秒差距 (km/s/Mpc) 67 公里。秒差距是天文学中使用的距离单位，大约等于 3.26 光年，即 30.9 万亿公里。兆秒差距是一百万秒差距。

paras.en: The second method is more direct, similar to the one used by Hubble in the 1920s when he first demonstrated that the universe is expanding.
paras.zh: 第二种方法更直接，类似于哈勃在 20 年代首次证明宇宙正在膨胀时使用的方法。

paras.en: It measures how fast distant galaxies are moving away from our home galaxy, the Milky Way, by observing the brightness of supernovae explosions in these far away galaxies.
paras.zh: 它通过观察遥远星系中超新星爆炸的亮度来测量遥远星系远离我们的家乡银河系的速度。

paras.en: Type Ia supernovae are known to be “standard candles” because we know that their luminosity is the same wherever they are. That means we can judge the distance to them from how dim they appear to us.
paras.zh: Ia 型超新星被称为“标准蜡烛”，因为我们知道无论它们在哪里，它们的亮度都是相同的。这意味着我们可以根据它们在我们看来的暗淡程度来判断它们的距离。

paras.en: To determine their intrinsic brightness, astronomers use other standard candles, such as Cepheid stars, in the galaxies nearby. These observations, which use the Hubble and James Webb space telescopes, give a higher value of around 73 km/s/Mpc.
paras.zh: 为了确定它们的固有亮度，天文学家使用附近星系中的其他标准烛光，例如造父变星。这些使用哈勃和詹姆斯·韦伯太空望远镜进行的观测给出了大约 73 km/s/Mpc 的更高值。

paras.en: This difference between the two measurements is called the Hubble tension. The difference between 67 and 73 may seem small, but it is statistically highly significant. If both methods are correct, then our standard model of cosmology must be missing something important.
paras.zh: 两次测量之间的差异称为哈勃张力。 67 和 73 之间的差异可能看起来很小，但在统计上却非常显着。如果这两种方法都是正确的，那么我们的宇宙学标准模型一定遗漏了一些重要的东西。

paras.en: Where did cosmic magnetic fields come from?
paras.zh: 宇宙磁场从何而来？

paras.en: Magnetic fields are everywhere in the universe. Planets and stars generate their own fields, but gaps in our understanding emerge when we attempt to explain the much larger scale magnetic fields threading galaxies and clusters, and possibly even cosmic voids.
paras.zh: 磁场在宇宙中无处不在。行星和恒星产生自己的磁场，但当我们试图解释穿过星系和星团，甚至可能是宇宙空洞的更大规模的磁场时，我们的理解出现了空白。

paras.en: One long-studied possibility is that magnetism first arose in the very early universe, long before the first stars or galaxies formed. These so-called primordial magnetic fields have been studied for decades, and searching for their imprints in the cosmic microwave background and other data offers a way to probe the early universe and the extreme energies that would have generated these fields.
paras.zh: 一个长期研究的可能性是，磁性首先出现在非常早期的宇宙中，早在第一批恒星或星系形成之前。这些所谓的原始磁场已经被研究了几十年，在宇宙微波背景和其他数据中寻找它们的印记提供了一种探测早期宇宙和产生这些磁场的极端能量的方法。

paras.en: In 2011, two of us (Karsten and Tom) pointed out that primordial magnetic fields would influence recombination — when electrons and protons first combined to form neutral hydrogen — and the universe turned from opaque to transparent. The first light able to travel freely from that moment on is what we now observe as the cosmic microwave background.
paras.zh: 2011 年，我们两个人（卡斯滕和汤姆）指出，当电子和质子首次结合形成中性氢时，原始磁场会影响复合，宇宙从不透明变成透明。从那一刻起，第一束能够自由传播的光就是我们现在观察到的宇宙微波背景光。

paras.en: If present, primordial magnetic fields would speed up recombination by pushing and pulling on charged particles, making matter slightly clumpy. Where particles are more crowded, they are more likely to meet and form hydrogen.
paras.zh: 如果存在，原始磁场将通过推拉带电粒子来加速重组，使物质稍微团块。在粒子更拥挤的地方，它们更有可能相遇并形成氢。

paras.en: Shifting the moment when the universe becomes transparent changes the size of the observed patterns in the cosmic microwave background. This effectively alters the cosmic ruler used to measure distances and, in turn, the value of the Hubble constant inferred from the model, helping to ease the Hubble tension. Two of us (Karsten and Levon) demonstrated this effect in 2020 using a simplified model of recombination.
paras.zh: 改变宇宙变得透明的时刻会改变宇宙微波背景中观测到的图案的大小。这有效地改变了用于测量距离的宇宙标尺，进而改变了从模型推断出的哈勃常数的值，有助于缓解哈勃紧张。我们两个人（Karsten 和 Levon）在 2020 年使用简化的重组模型证明了这种效应。

paras.en: In our new paper, we used the first full three-dimensional simulations of the primordial plasma with magnetic fields embedded in it, tracking how hydrogen forms.
paras.zh: 在我们的新论文中，我们首次对嵌入磁场的原始等离子体进行了完整的三维模拟，追踪氢的形成方式。

paras.en: We used the hydrogen formation history found through these simulations to compute predictions for how cosmic microwave background should appear if there were primordial magnetic fields, and tested these predictions against observations of the background.
paras.zh: 我们利用通过这些模拟发现的氢形成历史来计算预测，如果存在原始磁场，宇宙微波背景应该如何出现，并根据背景观测测试这些预测。

paras.en: The cosmic microwave background is extraordinarily sensitive to changes in recombination. If primordial magnetic fields altered it in a way that disagreed with observations, the idea could be ruled out. Instead, the data showed that our proposal remains viable.
paras.zh: 宇宙微波背景对复合的变化极其敏感。如果原始磁场以与观测结果不一致的方式改变了它，那么这个想法就可以被排除。相反，数据表明我们的建议仍然可行。

paras.en: Across multiple combinations of datasets, we find a consistent, mild preference for primordial magnetic fields, ranging from about 1.5 to three standard deviations. This is not yet a discovery, but a meaningful hint that they exist.
paras.zh: 在数据集的多种组合中，我们发现对原始磁场有一致的、温和的偏好，范围从大约 1.5 到 3 个标准差。这还不是一个发现，而是一个有意义的暗示，表明它们的存在。

paras.en: Equally important, the field strengths favored by the data, about five to 10 pico-Gauss today, are close to what would be needed for galaxy and cluster magnetic fields to originate from primordial seeds alone. A pico-Gauss is a unit used to measure the strength of magnetic fields.
paras.zh: 同样重要的是，数据支持的场强（目前约为 5 到 10 皮高斯）接近于仅源自原始种子的星系和星团磁场所需的场强。皮高斯是用于测量磁场强度的单位。

paras.en: Aside from helping ease the Hubble tension, if primordial magnetic fields are confirmed, they would open a new window into how the universe was when it was only split seconds old, perhaps offering a glimpse into important events such as the Big Bang itself.
paras.zh: 除了帮助缓解哈勃张力之外，如果原始磁场得到证实，它们还将打开一扇新的窗户，让我们了解宇宙在几秒钟前的样子，或许可以让人们一睹大爆炸本身等重要事件。

paras.en: Our results show that the proposal survives the most detailed test available today and provides clear targets for future observations. Over the next several years, we will learn whether tiny magnetic fields from the dawn of time helped shape the universe we see today and whether they hold the key to resolving the Hubble tension.
paras.zh: 我们的结果表明，该提案通过了当今最详细的测试，并为未来的观察提供了明确的目标。在接下来的几年里，我们将了解创世之初的微小磁场是否有助于塑造我们今天看到的宇宙，以及它们是否是解决哈勃张力的关键。
